description: The FloReST app is a prototype citizen and community science tool that lets residents report heavy rainfall and pluvial flooding, with photographs and locations, in the Ahr valley of Germany, which the July 2021 flood devastated. The FloReST research project built it with partners including Disy Informationssysteme, and described its design and field tests in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences, published on 20 April 2026. Coverage is the Ahr valley in Rhineland-Palatinate. Observations flow into a Geo Data Warehouse with dashboards for local authorities. Format and access: the article is open access, and the app source is on the GitLab server of Rhineland-Palatinate. Licence: the article is CC-BY-4.0; the code licence was not read. Caveats: a prototype whose limits include offline use and GNSS positioning accuracy. It supports emergency response and the collection of observed flood extents for hazard model checks. A related catalogue record is the German heavy rainfall hazard indication map.
